title: Sovereign Routing Gatekeeper for EU-only Residency and Tiered Fallbacks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a dedicated Routing Gatekeeper service that enforces EU-only data residency constraints, applies per-customer allowlists/denylists for regions and tiers, and selects fallback model variants when the primary region/tier is unavailable. This ticket covers the policy engine, decision API, audit logging shape, and the runtime adapters needed for low-latency enforcement in the serving path.

Background: Multiple customers require strict EU-only processing, some have contractually mandated dedicated capacity tiers, and platform autoscaling can attempt cross-region fallback when capacity is low. Current routing decisions are ad-hoc in several components; we need a single source-of-truth service that can make deterministic, auditable decisions with clear failure semantics (hard-enforce vs. soft-fail).

Scope:
- Policy model to express: EU-only residency, allowed regions per customer, denied regions, permitted tiers (hosted/dedicated/private), model variant fallback chains (e.g., quantized/cheaper fallback models), and emergency overrides for support.
- Decision API: synchronous gRPC/HTTP interface used by edge routers and runtime proxies. Must return decision, reasoning_code, and audit_token.
- Caching strategy: bounded TTL caches near proxies with policy-decision invalidation hooks. Sensitive policy changes (legal/contract) must expire caches immediately.
- Audit logs: structured, immutable events stored in the compliance bucket with fields: customer_id, request_id, decision, reason, region_chosen, model_variant, timestamp, policy_version.
- Rollout controls: feature-flagged canaries per customer, and a dry-run mode that logs but does not enforce to validate coverage.

Out of scope: long-term UI for policy editing (handled by separate PM ticket). On-prem private deployments will integrate via local policy sync; initial implementation will target hosted and dedicated runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: Decision API can evaluate residency and tier policies for a request and return a deterministic routing decision within 12ms p50 on staging
Policy language supports allow/deny lists for regions, tier access controls, and fallback model chains
Edge proxies use gatekeeper decisions in enforce mode for a subset of EU-only customers during canary
Audit events emitted for every decision and ingested into the compliance S3 path with required fields
Cache invalidation mechanism triggers within 5s after a policy change marked as 'contractual'
Dry-run mode shows divergent decisions in dashboard and creates a reconciliation report after 24h
implementation_notes: Policy model: implement a JSON/YAML-first policy schema with explicit semantics for 'hard_enforce' vs 'soft_fallback'
Decision logic: evaluate residency constraint first (if requires 'EU-only' then reject any non-EU region even if cheaper), then tier allowlist/denylist, then model variant fallback chain
Performance: colocate a small read-only policy cache in the runtime proxy; use gRPC streaming for policy invalidation hooks from Gatekeeper
Fallbacks: include 'compatibility attributes' on model variants (e.g., quantized-8bit, seq_len_limit) so Gatekeeper can choose compatible fallbacks, not just 'cheapest'
Circuit-breaker: add rate-limited fallback permission so when primary region is overloaded we can optionally route to an approved fallback variant marked as 'sovereign-approved'
Observability: expose metrics: gatekeeper_decision_latency_ms, gatekeeper_cache_hit_rate, gatekeeper_denied_requests_total, gatekeeper_fallbacks_used_total
rollout_plan: 1) Merge gatekeeper prototype behind feature flag (runtime and proxy adapters). 2) Dry-run for 48h for internal traffic; validate metrics and logs. 3) Canary: enable enforce mode for 3 pilot EU-only customers (with legal sign-off). 4) Iterate on policy expressiveness and perf. 5) Gradually expand to all EU-only customers; enable cache-invalidation for contract changes. 6) Post-rollout audit and runbook update.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased p95 latency in the serving path if decision API is remote — Mitigation: aggressive local caching and async refresh; keep p50 decision path local via cached policy
Risk: Incorrect policy leading to cross-border processing — Mitigation: strict test suite with contract-boundary tests and mandatory legal review for contractual policies
Risk: Policy churn causing cache thrash — Mitigation: batch policy updates and provide TTL/etag guidance to PM/legal teams
Risk: Fallback to incompatible model variant harms quality — Mitigation: require compatibility metadata and automated regression evals for any model entered into fallback chains

notes: PM feedback (2025-11-06): Ensure dry-run exposes mismatches to customers before enforcement. Add reconciliation report output for customers.
Design feedback (2025-11-08): Keep policy DSL small; prefer composable predicates over Turing-complete rules to simplify audits.
Security review (pending): encryption of audit_token in transit, HMAC-signed policy versions for runtime verification.
